messages:
sanjay: heads up — did a sweep on INT8 weight-only configs this morning (AWQ vs GPTQ, group-size sweep, packing toggles). saw a surprising p95 regression on chat endpoint after the kernel selector started preferring the new fast-int8-kernel. numbers below.

liz: can you paste the exact run command and env?

sanjay: run: `./run_perf.py --model redwood/7b-int8-weightonly --quant awq --group 32 --packing on --kernel-chooser=auto --seq 2048 --batch 1`

sanjay: results (local perf VM, a100-sxm):
```
baseline (group 16, packing off, kernel=fast-fp16): p50=22ms p95=40ms p99=120ms
experiment (group 32, packing on, kernel chooser auto picked fast-int8-kernel): p50=24ms p95=72ms p99=210ms
cpu% shows more memcpy/pack time, KV cache miss rate up ~3%
```

mike: hmm, so kernel chooser moved to the int8 kernel but latency got worse. Could be pack/unpack overhead or the kernel's tail-loop scalar path for group=32. Did you profile per-op?

sanjay: yup. perf traces show two hotspots: `pack_weights()` and `kv_cache_write()` during generation step 1..8. stack snapshots: pack is 28% of time, kernel compute 44%, kv_write 18%.

anya: what about batcher heuristics? with group=32 packing increases memory refs — if batcher coalesces small requests into the kernel with many prefix tokens, KV cache copy cost grows. Any change to `batcher.max_idle_ns`?

sanjay: default is 2_000_000 (2ms). I didn't touch it. But I did see more small bursts: our chat endpoint traffic has short back-and-forth (seq 256 then 1024) so continuous KV flushes.

liz: could calibration have changed the kernel chooser cost model? i.e., after calibration we updated kernel throughput table and the chooser now overestimates int8 throughput for long sequences.

mike: yes — calibration used synthetic seq=128/2048 mix but the profiler used median throughput which hides pack overhead (which is per-weight, not per-token). The chooser needs a packing amortization term: amortized_pack_cost = pack_time / expected_calls_per_session.

sanjay: quick mitigation I tested: force `--kernel-chooser=prefer-fp16` OR set group=16. forcing fp16 gave p95=38ms (closer to baseline). group=16 with packing on gave p95=42ms but p50 slightly better.

anya: sounds like two levers: 1) tuning the chooser model to include pack/unpack/kv copy amortization and sequence-length distribution, 2) change default group size heuristics per model shape. Also consider `pack-on-demand` (only pack when cached hot) vs eager pack.

perf-bot: automated profile uploaded: https://internal.perf.redwood/trace/1792501234/pack-kv-sweep (flamegraph + op timeline) :thumbsup:

mike: can we add a small experiment: run kernel chooser calibration with real traffic trace (not synthetic) and include new features: group_size, avg_prefix_len, pack_cost_per_param. Also run microbench for pack/unpack kernels with varying group sizes (8/16/24/32/48).

sanjay: already did a microbench. gist: pack_time per 1e6 params: group8=11ms, g16=7ms, g32=6.4ms, g48=7.9ms (so g32 best for pack alone). but combined with kernel scalar tail rewrite for g32 the compute kernel had higher cycles for seq>512. weird branch.

liz: maybe the int8 kernel uses a vector block size tuned for group multiples; branch divergence with tail tokens could be causing the kernel to regen fallback codepath. Did you check kernel fallback counters?

sanjay: yes: `kernel_fallback_count` spiked by ~600 for that run. Traced to `fast-int8-kernel::emit_tail_fallback` when tokens%block != 0 and group-size interacts with hidden_dim alignment.

anya: ok actionable list: 
- add `pack_amortization` to kernel chooser cost model (sanjay)
- add a guard to prefer non-int8 kernel when `kernel_fallback_count` > threshold (mike)
- run traffic-calibration job with real request traces for 24h (liz)
- consider pooling KV cache buffers to avoid per-request memcpy in `kv_cache_write` (sanjay/eng-infra)

mike: also propose a quick hotfix: set default group size=16 for AWQ in hosted for 7b and 13b until chooser update lands. Rolling that to dedicated could be optional.

liz: +1. schedule: who can own a short PR to change default group size?

anya: I can do PR for config change and add a flag `experimental.default_awq_group` so we can rollback quickly.

sanjay: I'll start a patch to chooser. minimal change: add `pack_cost_bytes` and `expected_session_calls` fields in profile JSON and re-eval. then rerun job.

mike: once patches land we'll run an A/B: control (current chooser) vs candidate (pack-aware chooser) on 10% traffic to verify p95/p99 impact. keep an eye on quality (int8 quant artifacts).

sanjay: one more note — GPTQ vs AWQ behaved differently: GPTQ kernels didn't hit the same fallback codepath (likely alignment differences) and had lower pack time but slightly worse llm quality in a couple prompts. include that in eval.

liz: great. append perf-bot output to the ticket. I'll spin up the calibration job. thanks everyone. :rocket:
